C-CHECKS-BINDING.title: The checks contract keys evidence to a head OID the provider neither accepts nor evaluates
C-CHECKS-BINDING.why: All three are one defect seen from three sides: the contract demands a commit key (TA-022), the corpus cannot say which of the two check families a row came from (TA-023), and the head OID is the wrong key even when it is available because Azure evaluates the merge (TA-024). One repair fixes all three: a declared binding kind per check row, plus the merge triple rather than a head fence for the review-bound family.

TA-035.title: cmd.forge.review.merge carries no merge strategy, and omitting one is not neutral
TA-035.promise: ADO-004 acceptance :140 'Async mutations expose ObservableWork and terminal provider receipts'; the brief's P4 - a request the service accepted is not a request the service finished.
TA-035.contradiction: The obvious reading is that the product cannot have the reported bug, because cmd.forge.review.merge carries no merge-strategy field and 'merge_strategy' returns zero matches in the forge schema. That reading is wrong: omitting MergeStrategy is not neutral. 'If MergeStrategy is not set to any value, a no-FF merge will be created if SquashMerge == false ... It is recommended that you explicitly set MergeStrategy in all cases.' So a strategy-less completion IS a noFastForward completion, and if the repository policy forbids no-fast-forward the request is refused. The Plans as frozen choose a strategy implicitly and cannot choose at all.

TA-007.title: A thread's anchor is a revision PAIR on Azure and the schema stores one ref

TA-011.contradiction: provider_adapter_profile.unsupported_reason_codes is typed as an array of non_empty_string, so the code every profile declares is not drawn from - and not checked against - the closed disabled_reason_code (54 members) or error_code (58 members) enums that every other reason in the corpus must come from. Azure's declared policy_scope_missing is in neither.
my_additional_findings: THE UNION'S SUPPORTING CLAIM IS FALSE. It says the same field holds missing_scope (GitLab) and pipeline_disabled (Bitbucket), 'which ARE enum members'. Verified on main: missing_scope IS a disabled_reason_code member; pipeline_disabled is in NEITHER disabled_reason_code NOR error_code. The corrected finding is stronger and NOT Azure-specific: the field is unchecked for every provider, and at least two of three non-Azure declarations are also off-enum.
TA-011.repair: Type the field against the closed enums (or state plainly that it is a free vocabulary). Lands in the common forge schema, not the Azure owner.

TA-012.title: policy_scope_missing is a read-side reason the Azure service cannot produce
TA-012.promise: ADO-002 acceptance :76 'Organization/collection, project, repository, policy and build access failures remain distinguishable.'
TA-012.contradiction: The Services fixture declares policy_scope_missing, but Azure DevOps has no read-side policy permission: the Git Repositories security namespace's policy bits - EditPolicies, PolicyExempt, PullRequestBypassPolicy - are all write/exempt/bypass, and reading policies rides on repository read; the evaluations endpoint lists exactly one OAuth scope, vso.code, the same scope that reads code. 'I can see this repository but not its branch policies' is not a state the service has; a caller who got policy_scope_missing would already have been denied at the repository.

provider_source_verifications.finding: Git Repositories security namespace 8adf73b7-389a-4276-b638-fe1653f7efc7 publishes PolicyExempt, EditPolicies and PullRequestBypassPolicy - all write/exempt/bypass, no read bit; policy/evaluations lists only vso.code

TA-012.repair: Remove or re-scope the reason code to the write/bypass paths, and say in ADO-002 which of the two the distinguishability promise means. Fixture edit plus one clause.

TA-013.title: Nothing in the corpus forbids client-side policy scope resolution
TA-013.promise: Section 0 :11 policy identity survives the mapping; the brief's policies/checks sentence.
TA-013.contradiction: The Plans constrain the OUTPUT of the policy mapping and say nothing about the DERIVATION. No statement requires provider-side applicability resolution, no prohibition on client-side scope resolution exists, and policy scope levels, matchKind and refName matching appear nowhere. An implementer who reads only the Plans, reaches for the obvious-looking collection endpoint and filters it client-side has violated no written constraint and produces a confident single WRONG answer, not an error - so no reason code fires and 'partial data is never complete' never gets a chance to apply.

provider_source_verifications.finding: git/policy/configurations is api-version 7.1 with repositoryId, refName, policyType, $top, continuationToken; policy/evaluations is 7.1-preview.1 with artifactId, includeNotApplicable, $top, $skip

my_additional_findings: FileSafe.md:225 verbatim: 'if canonical-root or scope resolution fails for a request, that request fails closed rather than guessing a case mode or write scope'
TA-013.repair: One negative constraint on the Azure owner, modelled on FileSafe.md:225: policy applicability is resolved by the provider's scope-resolving endpoint and never client-side; a failed resolution fails closed.

TA-016.title: policy_resource_id cannot express a scoped policy and expected_policy_revision cannot fence a set
TA-016.promise: ADO-003 :99 'branch-policy/check identities'; the brief's policies/checks sentence.
TA-016.contradiction: cmd.forge.repository.policy.preview requires policy_resource_id, provider_patch_ref and expected_policy_revision, and identifies its subject with ONE opaque string whose only worked example in the corpus is 'branch-policy:main' - keyed by branch name. Azure's identity is PolicyConfiguration.id plus the settings.scope[] entry that made it apply, and two different configurations can both be 'the branch policy on main'. The provider's own write path already addresses individual configurations by id (autoCompleteIgnoreConfigIds). expected_policy_revision is a single scalar while PolicyConfiguration.revision is per-configuration, so one scalar cannot fence a set whose membership can change without any member's revision changing.

provider_source_verifications.finding: autoCompleteIgnoreConfigIds verbatim: "List of any policy configuration Id's which auto-complete should not wait for. Only applies to optional policies (isBlocking == false). Auto-complete always waits for required policies (isBlocking == true)."
PolicyConfiguration carries isBlocking, isEnabled, isDeleted, revision (number), id (number) and type

TA-029.title: api_compatibility.endpoints cannot hold a per-endpoint API version
TA-029.promise: ADO-004 canonical_text :132-133 'API compatibility pins Services or Server variant, host/version, adapter/catalog, endpoints/scopes/features and rate.'

TA-030.title: Applicability and status are two capabilities with different keys and different maturity
TA-030.promise: ADO-002 canonical_text :68 'Azure DevOps Server capabilities require a current signed host/version support entry'; ADO-004 :133 'unknown mutations fail closed'; the brief's P3.
TA-030.contradiction: Which policies apply is branch-keyed (repositoryId, refName) at GA 7.1; whether each passes is review-keyed (projectId, pullRequestId) at 7.1-preview.1. The frozen Plans treat 'checks' as ONE capability, so an Azure DevOps Server host whose probed API set lacks the preview evaluations endpoint has no way to say so: it must either infer status from the PR's merge status or show an empty check list, both of which the corpus forbids elsewhere.

TA-033.title: The project GUID is a second required identifier, not a spelling of the project name
TA-033.promise: ADO-001 canonical_text :36-37 'Project is mandatory and no path, remote URL, display name or focus may replace the hierarchy'; section 0 :11 'The project identity is mandatory and cannot be collapsed'; section 7.1 :213 'Missing project or variant is needs_binding.'
TA-033.contradiction: The repository gets two identifiers - a human repository_slug AND a required provider_repository_id - and the project gets one. A literal search of the whole corpus for 'provider_project_id' returns ZERO files. Both identifiers are required in the same Azure request in different slots: the route path takes 'Project ID or project name' while the policy artifact template is vstfs:///CodeReview/CodeReviewId/{projectId}/{pullRequestId}, which needs the GUID. A missing project GUID produces a well-formed URL, a 200 response and an empty list - renovate's own test asserts the literal 'vstfs:///CodeReview/CodeReviewId/undefined/${pullRequestIdMock}'.

provider_source_verifications.finding: The policy artifact template is vstfs:///CodeReview/CodeReviewId/{projectId}/{pullRequestId}; renovate's own test asserts the literal "vstfs:///CodeReview/CodeReviewId/undefined/${pullRequestIdMock}"

my_additional_findings: NEW LEG THE UNION MISSED, and the cheapest one on the whole list: repository_locator.project is typed {type: [string, null]} while being in the `required` list. A binding can therefore carry an explicit null project TODAY and still validate - a direct contradiction of ADO-001's 'Project is mandatory' that the negative fixture (which OMITS the key rather than nulling it) does not catch. Dropping `null` from the type is a two-character fix.
TA-033.repair: Make provider_project_id required and GUID-shaped for azure_devops, obtained from a provider resource and never parsed from a URL; a binding without it is needs_binding. Separately, drop null from repository_locator.project.

TA-002.title: An unmapped provider revision cause must never render as a push
TA-002.promise: ADO-003 negative constraint :118 against flattening; the brief's P1.
TA-002.contradiction: The provider publishes seven revision causes with an EMPTY description for every one, and the reference client collapses anything unrecognised to the most reassuring one: IterationReason is bit-valued with Push = 0, and the accumulator is `if (resultPart) { result |= resultPart; }`, so an unrecognised name contributes nothing and the result stays 0 = Push.

provider_source_verifications.finding: IterationReason publishes exactly seven values, bit-valued, with Push = 0: {Push=0, ForcePush=1, Create=2, Rebase=4, Unknown=8, Retarget=16, ResolveConflicts=32}
The node client accumulator is `if (resultPart) { result |= resultPart; }`, so an unrecognised enum name contributes nothing and the result stays 0 = Push

my_additional_findings: RECLASSIFIED to an optional capability. The corpus as frozen has NO revision-cause field at all, so nothing can currently render as 'push' and there is no promise this defect can falsify. The proposition's repair - persist the provider's stated cause verbatim as a raw wire string alongside a typed one - adds a field to an additionalProperties:false object, which is a capability. It becomes landable as a correction only after TA-004 introduces a cause vocabulary.
TA-002.repair: Decision card: persist the raw provider revision cause verbatim, and render an unmappable cause as 'unknown cause' rather than any known one. Dependent on TA-004.
